skill.name: stale-record-audit
skill.description: Checks contacts from a CRM, spreadsheet, or CSV against Leadsets to flag possible job changes. Reports stored and returned values with check dates and requires approval before CRM write-back.
skill.summary: Flag possible title and employer changes in contact records before outreach.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The Leadsets endpoint is used for contact enrichment, but the workflow lacks an explicit approval step before it sends contact data. The other alerts concern Markdown, documentation links, service conventions, or output fields. No evidence of shell execution, host reconnaissance, environment access, or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Contact identifiers can leave the CRM before explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Before the first enrichment call, disclose the provider, record count, and fields to be sent. Require scope-specific approval and send only identifiers needed for matching.

semantic_findings.title: No Explicit Approval Before Contact Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The default scope includes up to 250 contacts in active sequences or their queues. The workflow can send contact identifiers to Leadsets before the user approves the disclosure. Report-only mode prevents CRM write-back, not external enrichment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The first probe can send a LinkedIn URL or domain, and the workflow then processes the remaining batch. Approval is explicit for multi-window plans and CRM write-back, not for the initial disclosure.

content.value_statement: Outdated titles and employers can make sales outreach irrelevant. This skill checks scoped contacts through Leadsets and reports possible changes with check dates.
actual_capabilities: Reads scoped contacts from a CSV or connected source and removes exact duplicates by record ID and email.
Checks Leadsets usage limits and tests the match on one contact before enriching the batch.
Classifies contacts as current, title changed, company changed, or could not confirm.
Reports stored and returned values with check dates and totals by status.
Can write flags as fields, notes, or tasks through a CRM connection after approval of the proposed changes.
limitations: Requires Leadsets access and a separate source connection for CRM or spreadsheet data.
Successful lookups consume enrichment records and are subject to service limits.
A missing or ambiguous match does not confirm whether a contact is still current.
Does not find replacement contacts or reverify email addresses already stored in the CRM.

use_cases.title: Review a Sequence Before Launch
use_cases.description: Check queued contacts for employer changes and review the flagged list before outreach.

use_cases.title: Audit Aging CRM Records
use_cases.description: Review records that have not been updated this quarter and prepare flags for CRM owners to approve.

use_cases.title: Check a CSV Before Import
use_cases.description: Separate confirmed changes, unmatched contacts, and incomplete rows before importing an older contact list.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Audit a CSV Sample
prompt_templates.scenario: Check a small file without changing the source.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit up to 20 contacts from this CSV. Before sending data to Leadsets, show me the fields you need and wait for my approval. Return a report only.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Review a CRM Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the contacts queued for the Q4 Expansion sequence in HubSpot. Confirm the scope and fields with me before sending contact data to Leadsets. Show old and returned titles and companies with check dates. Leave HubSpot unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Plan a Quota-Limited Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Schedule a contact audit that may need multiple usage windows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Count and deduplicate contacts in the attached CSV. Check Leadsets usage and propose batches that fit the current and weekly limits. Show the fields needed for matching and wait for approval before the probe. Report which contacts remain if a limit stops the run.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Prepare CRM Flags
prompt_templates.scenario: Review the exact change set before writing flags.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the Salesforce contacts assigned to my team that have not been updated in 90 days. Wait for my approval before sharing contact data with Leadsets. Show the exact notes you would add for confirmed employer changes. Wait for separate approval before writing anything.

output_examples.input: Audit 180 contacts from the Q4 Expansion sequence and leave HubSpot unchanged.
output: 131 current, 19 title changes, 14 company changes, and 12 could not confirm.
The report shows stored and returned values with check dates. No HubSpot records changed.

output_examples.input: Check 25 contacts from a CSV and show the proposed flags without writing them back.
output: Checked 22 contacts. Three rows lacked a company and were not auditable.
16 current, 2 title changes, 1 company change, and 3 could not confirm.
The company change report compares the stored and returned employers and includes the lookup date. No flags were written.

best_practices: Confirm your organization permits sending the selected contact identifiers to Leadsets before running enrichment.
Review the first match before processing the full batch, especially when names are common.
Review proposed flags and check dates before approving any CRM write-back.
anti_patterns: Assuming report-only mode keeps contact data inside the CRM.
Treating a missing match as proof that a record is current.
Treating catch-all or unknown email addresses as verified.

faq.question: Which contact sources can I use?
faq.answer: Use a CSV, Google Sheets, HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, or Attio. The agent needs its own access to the selected source.

faq.question: What information is needed for each contact?
faq.answer: Start with a name and company or company domain. A work email or LinkedIn URL can help distinguish contacts when a match is ambiguous.

faq.question: Does report-only mode keep my data in the CRM?
faq.answer: No. It prevents CRM write-back, but lookups still send contact identifiers to Leadsets.

faq.question: Which records are checked by default?
faq.answer: The default scope covers up to 250 contacts in active sequences or their queues. You can specify a different scope.

faq.question: What happens if Leadsets cannot confirm a contact?
faq.answer: The report marks that contact as could not confirm. It does not treat the stored title or employer as verified.

faq.question: Will the audit update my CRM or sequences?
faq.answer: The default is a report without source changes. CRM flags require approval of the proposed changes. The audit can recommend sequence changes for review.
